title: Edison Scientific Kosmos World-Model AI Scientist Generates Seven Cross-Domain Discoveries
aiSystem: Kosmos (World-Model Multi-Agent Scientist — Edison Scientific / FutureHouse)
whyItMatters: Introduced a structured shared world model coordinating parallel coding and literature agents across 200 rollouts (~42k lines of code & 1,500 papers per run), yielding 7 discoveries across four scientific fields.
summary: Released in November 2025 by Ludovico Mitchener, Angela Yiu, Benjamin Chang, Samuel G. Rodriques, Andrew D. White, and collaborators at Edison Scientific (FutureHouse’s commercial spinout), Kosmos solves long-horizon context drift in autonomous research agents by coordinating parallel data-analysis and literature-search agents through a persistent structured world model. Across 12-hour runs (~200 agent rollouts, executing ~42,000 lines of analysis code and synthesizing ~1,500 papers with line-level provenance citations), Kosmos produced seven highlighted discoveries spanning metabolomics, perovskite solar-cell materials science, neuroscience (flippase downregulation in vulnerable entorhinal neurons in Alzheimer’s), and statistical genetics (type 2 diabetes causal targets)—independently reproducing three unpublished/preprinted human studies while contributing four novel scientific findings.
technicalHighlights: Shared structured world model maintained coherent research trajectories over ~200 rollouts (averaging 42,000 lines of executed code and 1,500 papers per 12-hour session).
Independent domain scientists verified 79.4% of sampled report statements as accurate and rated a single 20-cycle Kosmos run equivalent to ~6 months of expert research time.

Reported 7 cross-domain discoveries spanning metabolomics, materials science, neurodegeneration, and statistical genetics—3 independent reproductions of hidden unpublished studies plus 4 novel hypotheses.
caveats: Preprint evaluation focuses on seven selected successful runs rather than an unselected universal success rate; independent evaluators noted ~20% statement error rates (especially in interpretive leaps) and external audits stressed the ongoing need for wet-lab validation and null controls.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated that coupling parallel literature and code-execution agents via an explicit world model unlocks coherent multi-hour autonomous scientific investigation.
scoreRationale.ripple: Influenced autonomous research-agent architectures across academic and commercial labs, proving discovery yield scales linearly with compute cycles.
scoreRationale.verification: Preprint with 79.4% independent statement accuracy and 3 blind reproductions of unpublished manuscripts, scored conservatively pending peer review and full wet-lab follow-up on novel claims.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed roughly 6 months of human cross-disciplinary data analysis and literature synthesis into a 12-hour overnight run.
